_comment: The rules the MetaHuman converter (mh_to_vrm.py) applies, as data so the Node tests and the Blender script read the same file. UE = an Unreal Engine 5 MetaHuman skeleton as the metahuman-to-glb pipeline exports it; VRM = VRM 1.0 humanoid bone and expression names. See docs/BUILD-2026-10-09-metahuman-nora.md.
_keepComment: Bones kept besides the humanoid ones: the chain links between them, so the spine and neck still bend through every joint. Every other bone (the 800-odd face-rig bones, twist and corrective helpers, finger-pad and metacarpal bones, toes past the ball) is removed and its skin weights move to its nearest kept ancestor. The face moves through its ARKit shapes instead.
_dropMaterialsComment: Face geometry that does not ship, matched as a case-insensitive fragment of the material name: M_Hide marks faces the clothes cover; the eye shell, lacrimal film, saliva and eye-edge are transparent overlays three.js draws as a grey film (metahuman-to-glb issue #19). The 5.7 pipeline names them MI_Face_EyeShell etc., the 5.6 one ada_facemesh_eyeshell_shader_shader etc.
_expressionsComment: VRM 1.0 preset expressions as weighted sums of ARKit shapes. Every bind is applied to every mesh that has a shape of that name (the face and the eyebrow cards both carry them). Visemes follow the usual ARKit-to-viseme blends; the weights are a starting point to tune by eye against the reference render.
_budgetComment: What the booth can carry on a phone (docs/REVIEW-2026-09-29-nora-dj.md asked ≤ 50k triangles and ≤ 8 materials of a commissioned model; a MetaHuman's face alone is 64k at LOD0, so these are the measured targets for the converter, checked by check-vrm.mjs).
